You see, you see, you see, you see, you see, you see, you see, you see, you see, you man, you see, you see, man, you've been playing with me so long, and people ask me them things. You see, it's not together.

Well you see, if you've got to organize a band, it's band together. You know what I'm talking about? You see? That's why I don't never change a man to my band. See, man, it's been so long, but man, man, you're the oldest of him in Saturday, the oldest of the band. Yeah, you see? Yeah, you see?

That's right. When you say the band get together, you know when you say the band gets together. Yeah. about? Tell me something Tommy. You know, I know you like to play for people dancing rather than listening. I know you told me that many times. Sure, yeah, quite. Sure. You know also the tempos, you play different tempos for dancing, not waltzes, I mean if you play just any kind of numbers.

So I like to play for dance. But see when I was in California, three weeks we played there in the club, we played for dance and that kind of dance flow there you know? That nice dance flow. So Mr. Bill said, well, what do you use if you say you're going to sue him, he's going to do nothing. You know what I mean? He ain't got no money. He ain't got no money. He ain't got all that kind of stuff you know. So listen, Mills now, I'm going to get back to Mills. Mills, now Mills was a nice boy, but Mills did a lot of smutty things you see. So man look, one night we was playing over there, you know. So there'll never be nothing, somebody said, Punchette said Mills was taping bands, you know, and bands didn't know they was taping them, you know what I mean? I said yeah. So I said nothing, you know. So we playing, you know. I happened to go back in that little room back there, you know. And I know that tape recorder, you know. So you know who's running? Who? That boy running. Mr. Bill, the boy from Canada. Ralph Cobb. Ralph! He is running to operate the door and things. Look, he's standing right by the door like that, you know. I was wondering, we were playing, you know, and I'm looking at him, I was wondering where the devil is standing by that door, it's so long, you know what I mean? You were in there, that's right. Where is he on the corner? Yeah, look, just look past the corner, going that way. Yeah, yeah. Nice lady, man. I sold her some records, you know me? So she said, said Mr. Tom, I heard what happened. I said, what happened? She started telling me about it. He said, Mills taped your band at you. He said, but he got one more tape for you, you know. I said, how you know? Oh yeah, he got one more. And sure enough, she wasn't lying. So she said, if you need any help, I'm with you, you don't mean to live. So Larry was living upstairs, the one bourbon, you know. So I was, one evening but this time evening. Larry rang up and said, say, kid, say, what you doing? I said, oh I'm not doing that. I said, after the time it come home, he wouldn't tell me what it was for, you know. He said, I said, yeah, I'll come home. So I went over there that evening and he still couldn't tell me, you know. He had to get the tape recorder. He had to get the tape recorder and he had to get to the tape recorder and he had to get That's what the tape, what you're going to have. Now look, you know how he got, I'll tell you how Larry got this tape, it was comical, man. So this guy played the guitar, you know what you're going to play the guitar? He played the guitar. Yeah, but anyhow the boy, the fella had made a tape. So Larry told the man if he said he was going to give the man a hundred dollars. You know what I mean?
All right.

So Anaheim, Mills he wanted the tape, he wanted to put it on the market, you see. So Larry said, well all right, I'll let you have it. See? So Mills keep on, you know, tired with the tape, didn't do nothing with it, so Larry asked him for the tape, asked him for it, you know. So he found it up. No he didn't have to put that tape in there, he was after keeping that tape, you know, I don't know. So when he put it in the wrong box, so Larry got it, you see. So after Larry got it, so I got it, I had a reunion, you know, with God from the president, you know.

He did a lot of, but he tape a lot of bands. What was the first band that you remember making any records from around here? Could you remember any of the bands? My band. Not my band, but with Millie Barnes and them. I don't mean the first- I don't mean the first record you made, I mean do you remember anybody else's band making records? Can you remember one?
